ai.description: This slender, green-bodied snake reaches 1.2 meters. It features a pointed snout, a distinct horizontal pupil, and a pale ventrolateral stripe. It is distinguished by its elongated, whip-like form.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ahaetulla laudankia* is best distinguished by its unique, distinctively patterned "checkered" or "tessellated" ventral scales, which differ from the uniform coloration of other Indian *Ahaetulla* species.
ai.habitat: *Ahaetulla laudankia* inhabits the moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests of the northern Eastern Ghats, typically found in dense canopy vegetation at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Laudankia Vine Snake is primarily diurnal, using its slender, cryptic body to remain perfectly still among foliage while waiting to ambush small lizards and frogs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla laudankia* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 4–11 young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with births observed between August and October.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla laudankia* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of Odisha, India, specifically inhabiting moist deciduous forests at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
